USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Urinary symptoms

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

An older man with bladder outlet obstruction begins an inhaled antimuscarinic bronchodilator. He subsequently has increasing difficulty passing urine. Which recognized adverse effect should be considered when reviewing his ipratropium treatment and other medicines?

  1. Direct stimulation of bladder contraction
  2. Urinary retention
  3. Osmotic diuresis
  4. Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus
  5. Acute uric acid overproduction
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Urinary retention

Antimuscarinic effects can worsen urinary retention, especially with outflow obstruction.

Understanding the options

Urinary retention
Antimuscarinic effects can worsen urinary retention, especially with outflow obstruction.
Osmotic diuresis
This would increase urine output rather than obstruct voiding.
Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus
This causes high-volume dilute urine.
Acute uric acid overproduction
This does not explain the antimuscarinic association.
Direct stimulation of bladder contraction
Muscarinic blockade inhibits rather than stimulates detrusor contraction.
